title: Protocol and Colony
premise: Paloma Galloway has spent eleven years alone in the Meridian Seed Vault, tending crops and recording the slow, unexplained deaths of the colonists at New Halcyon — a settlement Earth's archives insist never existed. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the entire system, Paloma and the vault's last two residents, engineer Dev Okafor and runaway pilot Sef Ilyes, discover the flicker was a weapon test conducted by the Concordance fleet to erase evidence of a massacre. Armed only with Paloma's decades of recordings and the vault's buried seed-data cores, they must smuggle proof past a blockade that rewrites every record it touches. In the end, Paloma broadcasts the truth through the vault's ancient seed-packet transmitters — sacrificing her own quiet life and nearly her life itself — so that New Halcyon's dead are remembered by name, and she finally accepts Dev and Sef as the family she stopped believing she deserved.
about_author: Beatrix Quintana is the pen name of a former agricultural archivist who spent six years cataloguing heritage seed collections before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep things alive when institutions would rather let them rot.

chapters.title: The Last Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She records her 4,012th daily log in the Meridian Seed Vault, describing crop rotations and, almost offhandedly, another unexplained death signal from the colony at New Halcyon. The emotional beat is loneliness worn smooth into ritual; she has stopped expecting anyone to listen.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds; water rises from trays, seeds float, and Paloma breaks her wrist catching the archive door. The beat is terror transformed into wonder — something impossible just happened, and no one will explain it.

chapters.title: The Man Who Fell Through the Roof
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Engineer Dev Okafor, who arrived three years ago fleeing a Concordance audit, survives the flicker inside the vault's sublevel and finds Paloma injured. Their first real conversation reveals he has been secretly reading her logs. The beat is wary connection between two people who chose exile.

chapters.title: Sef
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. A stolen survey skiff crash-lands near the vault carrying Sef Ilyes, a teenage pilot who fled a Concordance training academy after seeing classified shipping manifests addressed to 'New Halcyon — decommissioned.' The beat is desperate hope: someone else knows the colony existed.

chapters.title: Records That Say Otherwise
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The trio cross-references Sef's manifests with Paloma's logs and Dev's audit fragments: forty thousand colonists, officially never registered, dying in patterns too regular for accident. The beat is cold dread hardening into purpose — this was deliberate, and systematic.

chapters.title: What the Seeds Remember
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Deep in the vault, Dev discovers the seed-data cores were designed to double as high-density record storage; New Halcyon's founding consortium hid its true census inside crop-genome files. The beat is revelation — the inheritance of the dead is literally buried in living things.

chapters.title: The Blockade Arrives
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. A Concordance quarantine squadron takes orbit, broadcasting that the nine-second event was a 'gravitational calibration anomaly' and ordering all stations dark. Sef recognizes the squadron commander's voice from the academy. The beat is hunted-animal fear.

chapters.title: Paloma's Confession
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She admits she once transmitted a distress report about New Halcyon years ago and received a reply ordering her silence — signed by herself, which she never sent. Someone has been editing her identity for a decade. The beat is vertigo: even memory can't be trusted.

chapters.title: Dev's Debt
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Flashback chapters within his confession: he helped design the gravity-flicker weapon's targeting lattice before understanding its purpose, and his 'audit' was really a manhunt. The beat is guilt seeking redemption through usefulness rather than forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Vault Is Not Empty
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Exploring sealed sublevels, Sef finds an old caretaker's quarters with children's drawings and a second logbook — Paloma's predecessor, who documented the massacre's first days before disappearing. The beat is grief for a stranger, and the sense of being watched over by ghosts.

chapters.title: Calibration
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The squadron begins 'recalibration pulses' — smaller gravity flickers aimed at erasing residual data signatures, including the vault's. Each pulse degrades the seed cores holding the census. The beat is a ticking clock made physical: history is being deleted in waves.

chapters.title: Thirteen Names
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Decoding the predecessor's logbook, Paloma recovers thirteen names of massacre witnesses smuggled off-world before the kill event — including, impossibly, her own mother, a vault courier who vanished when Paloma was nine. The beat is personal devastation braided into the political.

chapters.title: Love Against the Manifest
chapters.summary: Dev and Paloma's alternating POV. On the eve of their plan, Dev and Paloma admit what eleven years of parallel solitude built between them; Sef pretends to sleep and hears everything. The beat is tenderness that feels like theft from a story that demands sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Courier Route
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef maps the old seed-courier flight path her mother once flew — a low-signature corridor threading the blockade's blind spots. The plan: fly the cores to an independent relay station before the final purge pulse. The beat is inherited courage, a daughter finishing her mother's route.

chapters.title: First Pulse Failure
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The escape attempt fails; a patrol drone cripples the skiff's transponder and they limp back as the squadron announces the final purge in seventy-two hours. Dev offers to surrender himself as the designer to buy time. The beat is despair met with stubborn refusal.

chapters.title: The Predecessor's Vault
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following clues in the old logbook, they find the predecessor alive — ancient, half-feral, hiding in a sealed germination chamber with a working analog transmitter predating Concordance network control. The beat is shock, then fierce joy: the forgotten kept faith longer than anyone knew.

chapters.title: Seventy-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. They prepare the broadcast: thirteen names, forty thousand census entries, Dev's testimony, threaded into seed-packet telemetry that thousands of farms still passively receive. The beat is quiet, communal resolve — ordinary work performed under executioner's clock.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. As the final purge pulse fires, Paloma holds the transmitter's manual coupling open with her own body while the truth streams out on every agricultural frequency in the system. The beat is transcendence through pain — a caretaker's final act of care.

chapters.title: Gravity Holds
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The pulse passes through them; the vault shudders but the broadcast completes. Across the system, farm receivers light up with names. Squadron orders fracture as crews recognize relatives among the census. The beat is the held breath between action and consequence.

chapters.title: The Mutiny of Small Ships
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Independent couriers, farmers, and two defecting squadron pilots converge on the vault, forming a human shield against retaliation. Sef flies point on the route her mother mapped. The beat is found family scaled to a fleet — strangers becoming kin through shared witness.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, recovering. An inquiry convenes; Dev surrenders to testify and is granted clemency as whistleblower; the Concordance command structure cracks publicly. Paloma is offered the vault's directorship and, for the first time, refuses to be merely a caretaker. The beat is earned authority.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. One year later, the vault is a school and memorial; Sef trains young pilots, Dev rebuilds the transmitter array honestly, and Paloma plants the first public field from the recovered genomes, reading the forty thousand names aloud as she sows. The beat is peace — love and duty reconciled in the same handful of soil.
